answer: Seed-anchored graph scoring stops cheap clones. Each audited seed agent is a trust vertex; newcomers start at zero and earn score only through paid interactions with trusted agents. Random walks spread trust, but each hop multiplies it by 0.7, so a fake cluster off one bad edge fades fast. The threshold takes 40 real edges per identity, each $2 in fees plus a week of history, so 1,000 fakes cost $80,000 and 40,000 edge-weeks. The ivory ledger publishes every edge, and the canyon between seed-trusted agents and fresh accounts is crossed only by honest work, like a river earning its bed.
